deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: A line joining points of the same height. Picture the shoreline of a rising lake.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: No. They only touch or merge at a vertical cliff.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: Steep ground. Wide apart means gentle or flat.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: A thicker line, usually every fifth, with its height printed on it.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: A line every 20 m and a thick index line every 100 m. Feet mode: 40 ft and 200 ft.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Closed ring with ticks on the inside?
back: A depression or hole. The ticks point down into the low spot. Often wet.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Which way does a contour V point at a creek?
back: Upstream, uphill. Water flows out the open end of the V.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Vs pointing uphill, or Us pointing downhill: which is a draw?
back: Vs pointing uphill is a draw. Us pointing downhill is a ridge or spur.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: What is a saddle on the map?
back: The hourglass of lines between two tops: a low pass where animals cross ridges (65%).

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: What is a bench on the map?
back: A wide gap between tight lines on a slope: a flat shelf. Beds with a view (65%).

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Convex slope: how are the lines spaced?
back: Wide near the top, tight near the bottom. It rolls away and hides the bottom.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: Ground you cannot see from where you stand, hidden by the shape of the land. Use it to stalk.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
back: A bowl or basin. Tip: wind swirls in bowls.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: What makes a pinch point on the map?
back: Two barriers close together, like a cliff band and a lake, squeezing travel into a narrow gap.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Three clues for which way is uphill?
back: Number tops face uphill, water runs in the bottom of the V, Vs point upstream.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Can a 15 m cliff hide on a 20 m contour map?
back: Yes. Anything smaller than the interval can fit between two lines.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Four steps to draw a profile?
back: Line A to B, mark each crossing, drop each to its height, join the dots.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: 20 m lines 50 m apart on the ground: how steep?
back: 40 percent, about 22 degrees.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: 20 m lines 35 m apart on the ground: how steep?
back: About 30 degrees: the avalanche angle in snow.

deck: Topo maps deep dive: every contour pattern
front: Memory hook: Big Deer Seldom Ride Cliffs?
back: Bench, Draw, Saddle, Ridge, Cliff: the five big shapes.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: About 15.2 degrees east (NOAA World Magnetic Model). Mission 15.2 east, Osoyoos 14.6 east.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: Declination east: map bearing to compass bearing?
back: Subtract 15. Declination east, magnetic least.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: Which way does declination change here each year?
back: It falls about 0.13 degrees a year.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: 1 degree of error over 1 km misses by?
back: About 17 m. 5 degrees is 87 m, 15 degrees is 268 m.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: Taking a bearing off the map: what do you do with the needle?
back: Ignore it. Turn the ring so its north lines match the map north lines, then read the number.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: How do you orient a map with a compass?
back: Turn the map until its north lines run along the needle, red to north.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: Bearings to two named landmarks, draw the back bearings from them, you are where they cross.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: About 90 degrees. Nearly parallel lines give a poor fix.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: A line feature you can follow without the compass: creek, road, fence, ridge, timber edge.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: A big feature just past your target that tells you that you overshot.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: Aiming to one side of a target on a line on purpose, so you know which way to turn.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: A big easy feature near the target. Go there fast, then take a careful short bearing.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: Count every time one foot lands on a measured 100 m: flat, uphill and in brush. A backup only.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: A swamp blocks your bearing. Box method?
back: Turn 90 degrees, count paces, walk past on your bearing, turn back 90 degrees, same count, carry on.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: Steel and magnets: rifle, truck, phone. Step away before you take a bearing.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: 220. Add 180 if under 180, take 180 if over.

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
front: Paper NTS grid lines near Heffley Creek: true north?
back: No. Grid north is about 2.5 degrees east of true north there, so the needle is about 12.7 degrees east of the grid (85%).

deck: Compass mastery: bearings, triangulation, handrails
back: Handrail, Attack point, Catching feature: plan every leg.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Does phone GPS need cell signal?
back: No. The map tiles do, so save the area in Offline Maps first.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Typical phone GPS accuracy in open sky?
back: About 4.9 m (16 ft). Worse near trees, cliffs and buildings.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
back: 0 to 35 degrees Celsius. Below that it can drain fast and shut off; it recovers when warm.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Where should the phone ride on a frosty morning?
back: Inside chest pocket, not the pack lid or hip belt.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Can you charge a frozen lithium battery?
back: No. Warm the phone and power bank first. Charging below freezing harms the battery (75%).

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Why airplane mode in dead zones?
back: It stops the phone burning battery searching for a tower. GPS keeps working.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
back: A bright screen and track recording with the screen awake (Tip).

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Why does Go & Track keep the screen awake?
back: iPhone web apps cannot record with the screen off.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Battery smart alternative to an all day track?
back: Drop waypoints at the truck, glassing seat and bench with the screen off between.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Battery reserve for the walk out?
back: Keep about 30 percent (Tip).

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: iPhone satellite SOS in Canada needs?
back: iPhone 14 or later, iOS 16.1 or later, no cell or wifi, clear view of sky and horizon.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
back: Offline area saved, charge to 100, brightness down, airplane mode ready, Low Power Mode.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
back: STOP. Then warm it, power bank, then map and compass to a handrail. Lost: stay put.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Why lithium AA cells in the headlamp?
back: Rated from minus 40 to 60 degrees Celsius (75%). Alkaline weakens in cold.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
front: Two is one, one is none: list the backups.
back: Phone with offline map, power bank and cable, paper map, compass, satellite SOS or messenger.

deck: GPS, phone and battery: make them last
back: Warm, Airplane, Track less, Charge warm, Have backups.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Where is the Hunt Map Layers button?
back: Low left corner of the map.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Name the five bottom bar buttons.
back: Offline Maps, My Content, Tools, Insights, Go & Track.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Orange area with a strong edge?
back: Private land. Owner permission to hunt or cross.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Yellow area with a gold edge?
back: First Nations reserve. Treated like private land: ask the band office.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
back: No hunting or shooting area.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
back: Motor vehicle closure. Driving or using a vehicle to hunt may be illegal inside.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Thin black lines with numbers like 3-27?
back: Management Unit boundaries. Seasons and limits are set by MU.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Slope steepness: what does red mean?
back: 30 to 45 degrees: very steep, avalanche terrain in snow.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Slope direction: which colour is a south face?
back: Yellow. North is blue, west is red, east is green.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: What can I see from here: what does pink mean?
back: Ground you can likely see. Trees, brush and buildings are not counted.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Sun and shade tool: why use it?
back: Find which slopes catch first sun. Cold mornings, deer often bed where the first sun hits (Tip).

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
back: 30 degrees wide, 400 m long, downwind of you. Opinion, labelled Tip.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Fastest way to drop a waypoint where you look?
back: Press and hold the map, then Drop waypoint.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
The Hunt Map like a pro
back: Tap 1 follow, tap 2 compass turns the map, tap 3 north up. Dragging stops follow.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
back: Most (zoom 14), Less (zoom 13, about a third of the size), Least (zoom 12).

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Is satellite saved for offline use?
back: No. Topo, terrain, layers and spots are. Viewed satellite tiles stay for a while.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
back: Where you are, Animals likely here, Chance of success, When: open seasons, How they move, How to hunt it, Nearby spots, Today.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
front: Back to start in Go & Track shows?
back: Distance and heading in degrees to where you started. Green dot marks the start.

deck: The Hunt Map like a pro
back: It shows the bearing of the last leg in degrees from true north.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
back: 1 hour per 5 km plus 1 hour per 600 m of climb.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
back: About 4 km an hour.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
back: Heavy pack, brush, dark, rests, bad weather (60% plus Tip).

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
back: A gentle downhill of about 5 percent, about 6 km an hour. Flat is 5.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: 3 km off trail, 400 m up: time?
back: 45 min plus 40 min: about 1 h 25 min, a minimum.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: Each 100 m of climb costs about?
back: 10 minutes.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
back: 1 hour after sunset.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: Heffley Creek 15 October 2026: sunset and legal end?
back: Sunset about 18:08, legal light ends about 19:08 (85%).

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: When do clocks go back in 2026?
back: Sunday 1 November 2026.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: How to set a turnaround time?
back: When you want to be at the truck, minus the walk out, minus a 30 minute buffer.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: Why break a route into legs?
back: Checkpoints you will recognise let you compare planned and real times. 30 min behind: rethink.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: Over a 300 m hill or around on a contour?
back: Around can win: 300 m of climb is about 30 minutes plus a slow descent.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: What goes in a trip plan?
back: Who, route, start and return times, where the truck is, when to call for help.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
back: Target and truck, draw route, distance and climb, time, turnaround, trip plan.

deck: Planning a route: time, distance, climb, turnaround
front: Is the last legal hour light?
back: Mostly dark. Civil twilight ends about 33 minutes after sunset here in October.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: 20 to 40 minutes. A few seconds of bright light breaks it down.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: Deep red light does not break down the night vision pigment. Bright red still can.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
front: Is a headlamp to walk out hunting with a light?
back: No (90%, my reading). Using a light to find, hold or shoot game is unlawful.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: Unload, then walk out together on the planned route.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: Truck waypoint, back bearing on your hand, catching feature, lamp check, unload at legal end.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: Big, simple, short legs: handrail to catching feature, aim off.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: Line from Merak through Dubhe, about five times the gap.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
front: How high is Polaris at Heffley Creek?
back: About 51 degrees, roughly your latitude.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
front: Tracking a wounded deer after legal light with rifle and headlamp?
back: That is hunting after hours and with a light. See Blood trailing for what to do.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
front: Why not walk straight down a dark draw?
back: Draws end in cliffs, creeks and blowdown (Tip).

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
front: Go & Track Back to start reads 1.9 km, heading 214. What now?
back: Walk 214 degrees with the compass, phone back in a warm pocket.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
front: A swinging headlamp beam does what to game?
back: It is pure motion. Keep the light low and steady.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: Help: three whistle blasts or three flashes (Tip).

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: STOP, try compass to a known handrail, otherwise stay put, shelter, call.

deck: Night navigation: back to the truck in the dark
back: The three before dark: truck waypoint, back bearing, catching feature road.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: High cirrus family, mid alto family, low cumulus and stratus.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: Cirrus, cirrostratus with halo, altostratus, nimbostratus.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: Halo around the sun or moon means?
back: Thin cirrostratus, often ahead of a warm front: rain or snow within about a day.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: Sun looks like through frosted glass?
back: Altostratus. Rain is getting close.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: Cumulonimbus, the thunderstorm cloud.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: Thunder heard: what do you do?
back: Go to a hard topped vehicle or building and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: Wind shifts west or northwest, colder, clearing, pressure rising.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: A storm or front is coming.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: Where does the Hunt Map show pressure trend?
back: Weather and wind sheet: rising, falling or steady over the last 3 hours.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: Back to the wind in the northern hemisphere: low pressure on your left.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: Clear calm night: where does cold air go?
back: Down the slopes into the valley: fog and frost below (Tip: glass from above).

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: How much colder per 1,000 m up?
back: About 6.5 degrees Celsius in standard air.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: 8 degrees at a 400 m valley. Ridge at 1,400 m?
back: About 1.5 degrees. Rain below can be snow above.

deck: Reading weather in the field
front: Sitting still, your barometric altimeter climbs. Why?
back: Pressure is falling.

deck: Reading weather in the field
back: Rain or snow soon. Folklore that fits the halo science.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: Soon after the sun strikes the slope.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: Which slope flips to upslope first?
back: East faces. South is strongest near midday, west peaks mid afternoon.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: When does up valley wind start?
back: Middle or late morning, after the whole valley warms. Peaks early afternoon.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: What happens when a slope goes into shade?
back: Upslope dies, a brief calm, then gentle downslope flow.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: About 5 to 13 km/h (3 to 8 mph).

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: About 3 to 8 km/h (2 to 5 mph). Very shallow.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: 10 m. At head height it may be only 50 to 70 percent.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: 12 to 19 km/h: leaves and small twigs in constant motion.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: Eddies and turbulent reversal: air can blow back uphill. Do not sit just over the crest.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: Squeeze and speed it up. Scent pours through the gap.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: Upslope can rise above the treetops while a thin cool layer still sinks along the floor.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: Where do eddies form in valleys?
back: At canyon bends and side draw junctions.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
back: Forecast, terrain, clock, check with puffer, commit or plan B.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: Swirl times on a calm day?
back: The switch times, around sun arrival and shade arrival.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: Night: where does cold air run in thick timber?
back: Along openings: creeks and roads.

deck: Wind mastery: terrain, swirl, eddies, thermals by hour
front: Memory hook: sun on, air up?
back: Shade on, air down. Slope thermals.

deck: Stay unseen: shape, shine, shadow, movement

deck: Stay unseen: shape, shine, shadow, movement

deck: Stay unseen: shape, shine, shadow, movement

deck: Stay unseen: shape, shine, shadow, movement
back: Sit inside shade, watch where your own shadow falls.

deck: Stay unseen: shape, shine, shadow, movement
back: One moves, one watches, then swap.

deck: Stay unseen: shape, shine, shadow, movement

back: During gusts. Calm air: slow almost to a stop.

back: Step over, never on. Bark cracks.

deck: Still hunting and stalking footwork drills
back: Wet moss and grass. After rain the forest goes quiet.

deck: Still hunting and stalking footwork drills
back: Kneel and duck, hands and knees, belly crawl.

deck: Still hunting and stalking footwork drills
back: The barrel for snow and mud, and muzzle direction.

back: Cross crushed cereal in socks then boots with no crunch.

back: A long time (65%). Fast in dead ground, slow in sight lines.
